note: An agricultural sales rep and pastor with four kids — employed, not a business owner, physician or equivalent, so 'successful' fails on the stated test even though he is plainly capable and disciplined. Income fails decisively and on the record: 'I know I can't. I can't spend $6,000.' Good-to-great fails too; he is closer to rescue than to optimisation — eight months of walking only since a hamstring injury, self-described as 'not the healthiest I want to be, so there's weight as well', and facing a clinician's fork between diet and starting medication for raised blood sugar. He does match on health being the neglected corner rather than a lifelong avoidance, and nothing suggests the 50-lb-overweight-and-gym-averse exclusion — he owns a squat rack and has trained since his teens. Most valuable here is that he rejected the ICP framing to the rep's face: 'People use the words business owner, entrepreneur, busy things, because then all of a sudden here comes the hammer for some stupid, ridiculous number... I have bills I have to pay. So it's not just successful and those type of things.' That is the stated ICP's income assumption being contradicted by a prospect who fits its lifestyle description.
